newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN GENDARMES FLY SHOTGUN OVER POSTMEN.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN GENDARMES FLY SHOTGUN OVER POSTMEN.

text.p: Belgian gendarmes have begun flying shotgun for the country's postmen who have been the target of a series of armed attacks in recent months, a spokeswoman for the gendarmerie said on Thursday.
"We had a flight yesterday and another one today," she said, noting that between March and October there had been 21 armed attacks on postmen.

Most of the attacks have taken place in and around the central Belgian town of Charleroi, a formerly thriving place but now largely an industrial wasteland in the heart of Belgium's impoverished Walloon region.

Charleroi leaped to world attention in August as the home of child rapist Marc Dutroux. Police rescued two sexually-abused young girls from a makeshift dungeon in one of his houses in the town and unearthed the bodies of four more nearby.
"Charleroi has always been a region of crime and armed robberies," the gendarmerie spokeswoman said.
Last week the gendarmes asked the country's postmen to help act as their eyes and ears to help fight crime. The postmen refused.
